subject: HeliumBio dedicated sizing playbook — context/KV cache & quantization options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Dedicated sizing playbook — quick kickoff and data request

Elena / HeliumBio ops team —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion I put together a concise playbook to size a dedicated pool for your NeoX-20B deriv (fine-tuned) with long-document use cases. Attached: brief workload summary (you provided), an initial KV sizing workbook, and a draft Redwood dedicated playbook with options.

High-level asks from you so we can finalize capacity and a reserved quote:
- Confirm 90/95/99th percentile context length distribution (you mentioned 12k average, can you confirm percentiles).
- QPS and peak concurrent sessions (steady vs burst windows).
- Target SLA (p50/p95 latency targets) and acceptable tail-latency behavior (drop vs degrade).
- Any firm constraints around quantization (do you need lossless up to a small eval delta or is 4-bit acceptable?).

Initial sequencing I propose:
1) Quick feasibility pass (this week) — feasibility matrix and preferred GPU class (H100 vs A100/L40S).
2) Two sizing options delivered (latency-first, cost-first) with explicit GPU counts, KV sharding plan, NVMe host-offload fallback, and rollout plan (canary + canary-sized routing).
3) Pilot: 2-week dedicated pilot on reserved pool with traffic mirroring for perf/quality checks.

I'll draft numbers once you confirm the distribution. Looping in Laura (ops scaling) and Aditya (model footprint/quant) — their notes are inline in the workbook.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: heliumbio_workload_summary.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing playbook — quick kickoff and data request

Vivek — thanks, sending the clarified numbers below and attaching a small sample trace.

Workload summary (finalized):
- Model: NeoX-20B fine-tuned (customer-specific LLM).
- Context percentiles: p50 ~ 3k tokens, p75 ~ 6k, p90 ~ 12k, p99 ~ 25k (very rare long docs).
- Average request size: 2.8k tokens (includes prompt + history).
- Peak concurrent sessions: 250 concurrent sessions during daily 30-minute ingestion windows; baseline steady concurrency ~ 40.
- QPS: baseline 18 QPS, peaks up to 85 QPS for short windows.
- Latency target: p95 generation latency < 600ms for typical requests (<=6k); for >12k we can tolerate progressive streaming but need stable tail behavior.
- Quality: we need <1% degradation in Rouge/BLEU across representative eval suite vs current on-prem model.

Procurement note: CloudInfra procurement is on the thread for resource approvals and any provisioned networking.

Attachment: heliumbio_sample_traces.ndjson (1 MB)

—Elena
Head of Platform Engineering
HeliumBio

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@heliumbio.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, procure@cloudinfra.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing playbook — quick kickoff and data request

Elena — great, that's exactly what we needed. Based on your percentiles and peak concurrency, we ran two initial sizing candidates. Below is an executive summary (technical details and calculations are in the attached heliumbio_kv_sizing.xlsx):

Option 1 — Latency-first (recommended for strict p95 target)
- Hardware: H100 80GB (NVLink per-host), dedicated pool with 24 GPUs (6 hosts x 4 GPUs)
- Model footprint (unquantized warm): ~38–45 GB GPU-resident for weights + runtime buffers
- KV cache: to support 12k contexts we plan KV sharding across 4 GPUs per session; effective KV memory per session ≈ 10–14 GB (total across shards; per-GPU approx 3–3.5 GB). p99 long docs (25k) will use streaming + partial NVMe offload.
- Concurrency: 250 concurrent sessions achievable by multiplexing across the pool; typical sustained concurrency ~40 uses small pools for quicker latency.
- Pros: meets p95 latency target for up to 6k requests without host fallback; predictable tail.
- Cons: highest $/token; larger reserved commitment.

Option 2 — Cost-first (aggressive quant + host-offload)
- Hardware: A100 80GB with NVMe bursting, 18 GPUs (6 hosts x 3 GPUs) as a reserved pool + 6 burst GPUs for peak windows
- Quantization: 4-bit asymmetric quant for weights (we recommend QAT-ish tuning), 8-bit for some attention kernels as fallback. We expect ~1–3% eval delta (need you to sign off on eval set).
- Model footprint (quantized): ~8–12 GB GPU-resident for weights depending on format + runtime buffers
- KV cache: kept mostly on host RAM with hot KV pages pinned to GPU; for 12k context expect ~6–9 GB host-side per active session, with parallel prefetching to amortize latency.
- Concurrency: supports baseline QPS and recommended reserved concurrency for steady windows; peaks require burst pool and routing rules.
- Pros: materially lower monthly cost (estimated ~35–45% savings vs Option 1), lower reserved GPU count.
- Cons: small quality delta; more complex ops (prefetching, NVMe fallbacks).

Operational recommendations
- Canary plan: start with 2 H100 nodes (8 GPUs) routing 10% mirrored traffic for 7 days (collect quality/regression metrics).
- Rolling fallback: if quantized variant underperforms on the eval suite, automatic fallback to non-quantized variant in 2-step A/B rollout.
- Autoscaling: use reserved baseline + short-duration burst capacity for the 30-minute ingestion windows; off-ramp scale in 10-min granularity.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency attribution per model version + prompt-set based quality monitors.

Next steps I propose:
1) You sign off on Option 1 vs Option 2 (or give priority weighting).
2) Redwood to produce a formal quote + exact reserved GPU counts and monthly cost breakdown (we'll include pilot discount).
3) Pilot schedule: provision networking and canary routing — target pilot start in 2–3 weeks.

Looping in Priyom for billing/commit sizing details (Priyom — if Elena picks Option 2, she will want an example pricing comparison chart with committed vs on-demand burst).

Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: heliumbio_kv_sizing.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing playbook — quick kickoff and data request

Elena — quick pricing sketch based on Vivek's two options. Numbers are intentionally rounded; formal quote will follow.

Option 1 (H100 latency-first):
- Reserved monthly cost (24 x H100 equivalents): ~$112k/month (includes networking, observability add-on).
- Expected pilot cost (2-week reserved pilot): ~$26k (pro-rated) + engineering support credits.

Option 2 (A100 quantized cost-first):
- Reserved monthly cost (18 x A100 equivalents + 6 burst): ~$68k/month base + $12k/month burst buffer (on-demand).
- Expected pilot cost (2-week reserved pilot): ~$14k (pro-rated).

Notes:
- Both options include 30-day retention for traces and 90-day for token accounting. Extended retention and compliance packaging are add-ons.
- We assume standard networking egress policies; any dedicated interconnects or cross-region peering will adjust prices.

If you want, I can prepare an apples-to-apples cost-per-1M-tokens comparison using your QPS/avg tokens figure.

—Priyom
Senior Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@heliumbio.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing playbook — quick kickoff and data request

Thanks — this is very helpful. High level decision: we'd like to pursue Option 2 (cost-first) with the following conditions:
- Redwood to run a pre-pilot evaluation: mirror 100k requests against the quantized variant to validate <1.5% quality delta on our eval set.
- Pilot must include NVMe offload configuration and an ops playbook for failover to non-quantized variant.
- Provide a detailed runbook for handling p99 long requests (25k) — we prefer streaming with partial KV eviction to NVMe (please include expected latency tail and token-throughput vs context size).
- CloudInfra procurement will coordinate PO terms for the reserved capacity; I'll route the PO once we have the formal quote and pilot SOW.

Next actions: Vivek/Aditya — please send a short pre-pilot plan (milestones + observability checks) by EOD Wednesday. Priyom — once we get the pilot SOW, please add the pricing appendix for committed vs burst usage.

—Elena
Head of Platform Engineering
HeliumBio
